sections.html:
Daphne sits in Baldwin County on the eastern shore of Mobile Bay, along Interstate 10 about 11 miles east of Mobile. It is the most populous city in the county and a principal city of the Daphne, Fairhope and Foley metro area. Locals group Daphne, Spanish Fort to the north and Fairhope to the south as the Eastern Shore. The land slopes gently from sea level on the west to low rolling hills inland, and no part of the city is more than about 150 feet above sea level.

The 2020 census counted 11,195 households in 12,157 housing units, with 7.9% of units vacant and a median age of 40.1. Homeowner vacancy was 2.4%, while rental vacancy was 10.6%. An owner with a rental house should expect a tenant search to take longer than a sale to a buyer who needs no tenant.

Hurricane Ivan, a Category 3 storm that made landfall near Gulf Shores in September 2004, caused widespread flooding and damage in Daphne. Summers are warm and wet, with July and August highs near 91 degrees and annual rainfall around 68 inches. Buyers on the coast ask about storm history, and the answers can change what they are willing to pay.

Before a sale, owners usually gather:

  • Flood zone information and any elevation certificate for the house.
  • Homeowner and wind or flood insurance policies and recent claims.
  • Roof age, shutters and window condition.
  • Records of past storm repairs, with receipts.

Expect a buyer to ask about insurance cost early. On the coast it often shapes the whole offer, so having current quotes in hand helps.

Daphne Utilities provides water, sewer and natural gas. Electricity comes from Riviera Utilities, based in Foley. The Daphne Fire Department and Daphne Police Department serve the city, and Baldwin Rural Area Transportation Service runs a bus. The city has no rail or air service, and Mobile Regional Airport and Pensacola International Airport handle most flights. Three exits from I-10 enter Daphne, at US 98, US 90 and AL 181.

Public schools belong to the Baldwin County Board of Education, and Daphne High School is among them. Private options include Bayside Academy, Christ the King Catholic School and Bayshore Christian School. Families often start a search by school, so say which one serves your address.

A mayor and a seven-member council, all elected every four years, run the city, with a semi-autonomous Utilities Board and a Zoning Commission in support. Questions about a lot, an addition or a rental go through the Zoning Commission and city hall. If you built a room or a porch, ask whether permits were closed out before you list.

Homes near the bay and the parks tend to be described by those landmarks. Village Point Park Preserve, May Day Park on Mobile Bay and the Daphne Sports Complex are the sort of places buyers use to picture daily life. Name the ones near your street in a listing or in your offer request.

Damage left from a past storm is one of the biggest obstacles on the Eastern Shore. A lender's appraiser may refuse to approve a house with an unrepaired roof or water damage, and a buyer using a loan can end up walking away. That can leave you with a signed contract that never closes and weeks lost.

Your options sit on a spectrum. You can repair first and list at full price, which costs money and time up front. You can list as-is and accept lower offers from buyers willing to take on the work. Or you can sell directly to a cash buyer who prices the damage in and closes without an appraisal. Gather the insurance claim file, photos taken before and after, contractor estimates and any receipts, and you will be able to compare the three honestly.

If an insurance claim is still open, tell the buyer and the closing agent. Who receives the payout, you or the new owner, has to be settled in writing before closing, and surprises on that point can stall a deal at the last minute.

A Baldwin County deed is filed with the probate judge, who figures the state recording tax at 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of that. The deed must show the actual purchase price, and a mortgage that already paid its own tax comes off the taxable amount.

Alabama property taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. Settle with your closing agent exactly who covers the current bill, and ask that it appear on the settlement statement.

A Daphne sale goes faster when these items are ready:

  1. The recorded deed, or estate papers showing who may sign.
  2. The latest property tax bill and a mortgage payoff letter.
  3. Flood zone and insurance documents.
  4. Receipts for roof work and storm repairs.
  5. Leases, if tenants live in the house.

Hand the closing agent a copy of the whole stack at the start. Any gaps will show up in the title search, and they are easier to fill while time remains. If an item is missing, such as an elevation certificate, ask the county or your insurer how to get a replacement, then keep the request in your files.

sections.h2: Selling a rental house with a tenant
sections.html:
Daphne's rental vacancy rate of 10.6% shows that empty rentals are common, so a tenant in place can be an asset or a headache depending on the lease. Collect the lease, the deposit records and the payment history. A buyer who wants to keep the tenant will ask for all three, and a buyer who wants the house empty will ask when the lease ends.

Talk to the tenant early. People who know the plan are more likely to allow access and keep the house tidy. If the lease runs past your preferred closing date, ask the buyer whether a later date works or whether they will take the house with the tenant still inside.

sections.h2: Listing or direct sale on the Eastern Shore
sections.html:
Sellers here usually weigh a listing against a direct sale. A listing can suit a turnkey house with a clean insurance history. A direct as-is sale suits a house with storm damage, an out-of-area owner or a probate case, and we buy houses in Daphne without commissions or closing costs to you.

The mix of families, retirees and commuters in Daphne means two kinds of buyers: households who want school zones and parks, and older owners who want to be near medical care. A listing reaches both, but it also exposes the house to insurance questions and repair requests. A cash offer sidesteps those and gives you a fixed date. Compare the two in writing before you choose, and ask what the buyer will do if the house has unresolved storm damage.

faqs.q: What county is Daphne, Alabama, in?
faqs.a: Daphne is in Baldwin County. It is the most populous city in the county.

faqs.q: Do hurricanes affect selling a house in Daphne?
faqs.a: They can. Hurricane Ivan in 2004 caused widespread flooding and damage in Daphne. Buyers ask about flood zones, insurance and past damage, so keep those records handy.

faqs.q: What is the Alabama deed recording tax?
faqs.a: It is 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction of $500, calculated by the probate judge when the deed is recorded, with mortgages that paid their own tax subtracted.

faqs.q: When are Alabama property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1, delinquent after December 31. Ask your closing agent who covers the current bill.
